This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 22.01.2015 Passed In Mvc
No.1059/2011 On The File Of The Xxi A.C.M.M & Xxiii

A.S.C.J, Mact, Bengaluru, Partly Allowing The Claim
Petition For Compensation And Seeking Enhancement
Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment
In this appeal, petitioner, apart from seeking enhancement, he has challenged the attributing of 40%
of contributory negligence passed as per order dated 22.01.2015 in Mvc No.1059/2011, by Xxi
A.C.M.M & Xxiii A.S.C.J, Mact, Bengaluru, (Scch-25) ('the Tribunal' for short).

2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before
the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 03.11.2010 at about 5.30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding the
motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-V-2758, as a pillion rider, rided by one Ramesh on Muthkur Cross,
Anugondanahalli Hobli, Hoskote Nc: 2024:Khc:32645 Taluk, Bangalore, Bmtc bus bearing
No.KA-01-FA-576 dashed against the motor cycle, due to which the petitioner fell down and
sustained injuries to his right Tibia.

After taking treatment at Vaidhehi Hospital and Sanjay Gandhi
Hospital, he has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.

Claim was opposed by the
Insurance Company.

After taking the evidence and hearing on both parties, the Tribunal by
impugned judgment assessed compensation of Rs.1,25,893/- for the reason of petitioner was under
the influence of alcohol.
Tribunal attributed 40% of the contributory negligence against him.
Aggrieved by the same the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Smt. Sree Vidya G.K, learned counsel appearing on behalf of Sri.
T.N.Viswanatha, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.T.Mohan Kumar, learned counsel for the
Insurance Company.

5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that, the petitioner is a pillion rider of the
motor cycle at the time of accident.

The Tribunal under wrong impression that, petitioner was under
the influence of the alcohol at the Nc: 2024:Khc:32645 time of accident, erroneously attributed
40% of contributory negligence.

The petitioner was not the rider of the motor cycle, there is no
principle of attributing contributory negligence on part of pillion rider.

There is no fault on the part
of the petitioner, complete negligence is on the part of the driver of the Bmtc Bus and for this
reason the driver was prosecuted and not the rider nor the petitioner.

It is further contended that
the petitioner has placed the medical evidence through Pw2, that he has suffered functional
disability of 19% due to malunion of the right Tibia.

But the tribunal has taken only 10% of the

disability, which is on the lower side and sought for enhancement.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company has contended that the medical records
points out that petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.

Because the pillion rider was
intoxicated, the rider was unable to ride properly and hit against Bus.

Tribunal ought to have
attributed complete negligence on the part of the petitioner.

However, attributed negligence 40%
only.

Compensation assessed should be proportionate to the nature of injury, fracture is not Nc:
2024:Khc:32645 affecting the earning capacity of the petitioner, and it is not a case for any
enhancement.

7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for both
parties and perused the records.

8. The material on record points out that there was an accident involving the motor cycle and Bmtc
bus in question on 03.11.2010 at 5.30 p.m., at Muthkur Cross in the limits of Hoskote Taluk,
wherein the petitioner being the pillion rider fell down and sustained fracture of right Tibia.

Medical
evidence also point out the malunion of the facture.

PW2-Dr.Prakash, Orthopedic Surgeon of Sanjay
Gandhi Hospital and also a treated Doctor, assessed the functional disability of 19% to the
petitioner.
Whereas, the Tribunal has taken it at 10%.

The Tribunal has taken the income of the
petitioner at Rs.5,000/- p.m.

In the year 2010, a person with no proof of income will earn not less
than Rs.5,500/- p.m.
Hence, notional income of the petitioner is not less than Rs.5,500/-p.m.

The petitioner is a plumber by profession, he is required to stand and sit to do the plumbing work,
though the permanent physical disability as per Tribunal is 19% having regard to facts and
circumstances functional disability at 15% instead of 10% as assessed by it.

The Tribunal awarded
Rs.5,093/- towards medical expenses and the same is kept intact.

Towards pain and sufferings
tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/-, it shall be Rs.25,000/-.

The petitioner was hospitalized for six days,
travelled to two hospitals and spent money towards incidental expenses.

Hence, it is considered at
Rs.10,000/- instead of Rs.5,000/-.

Loss of amenities is assessed at Rs.20,000/- as against
Rs.7,800/- assessed by the Tribunal, and petitioner laid up period for minimum of four months.

Hence loss of income during laid up period will be Rs.22,000/- (Rs.5,500/- x 4) as against
Rs.15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

As regards the loss of future income is concerned the income
of the petitioner is Rs.5,500/- p.m., and considering the age of petitioner as 50 multiplier '13' is
adopted, functional disability is treated at 15%, then it comes to Rs.5500/-x12x13x15% =
Rs.1,28,700/- hereby total compensation of Rs.2,10,793/- as against Rs.1,25,893/-
Nc: 2024:Khc:32645 awarded by the Tribunal and the enhanced compensation of Rs.84,900/-
rounded off to Rs.85,000/-.

10. As regarding liability is concerned on careful perusal of the evidence of driver of the Bmtc bus,
who asserted that the petitioner was not the pillion rider, but he was rider, under the influence of
alcohol dashed against the bus.
On the contrary the petitioner was not the rider of the motor cycle.

If
the petitioner was at fault why a police complaint was not filed against him as rider of the motor

cycle. Prosecution papers clearly point out that one Ramesh was the rider of the motor cycle, on his
complaint driver of the bus, has been prosecuted by the police.

sentences.text:
It goes to demonstrate that, complete
negligence was on RW-2/the driver of the Bus.
11.

The Tribunal considered the medical evidence and recorded the finding that the petitioner was
under the influence of alcohol, when he was admitted to the hospital.

Court cannot attribute any
negligence on his part without any evidence.

Hence, the finding recorded by the tribunal in
attributing 40% of contributory negligence on the petitioner being the pillion Nc: 2024:Khc:32645
rider is erroneous.

;
iv) The order of the tribunal attributing 40% contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner is hereby set-aside;
v) Respondents are liable to pay the entire compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
vi) Respondent No.1/Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the Insurer.
vii) Insurance Company shall deposit the full compensation with interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
